Ravi — thanks, glad to hear legal/procurement are lined up.

Below is a compact boarding checklist you can share with your infra team. I've attached an editable template (redwood-onprem-onboard-template.xlsx) and our standard security questionnaire.

Onboarding checklist (high level):
- Account & IAM: provide cloud account IDs (if cloud-peering) or a list of service accounts/keys for on-prem orchestration. Include owners and rotation windows.
- Network topology: planned CIDR(s), preferred NAT/egress model, and whether cross-account peering or private link will be used.
- IP allocation: static VIPs required for load balancer and healthchecks (see Marissa's note for ranges).
- Connectivity: VPN/Direct Connect options + bandwidth expectations; test/primary circuit details.
- Secrets & KMS: KMS key ARN or HSM vendor + access process; indicate if you need Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed only.
- Compliance evidence: SOC2 report, contact for audits, and retention window for logs/traces.
- Maintenance windows & RTO/RPO: proposed weekly maintenance windows and acceptable failover SLAs for the pilot.
- Certs & DNS: Subject Alternate Names you will publish; TLS termination preference (customer vs redwood).
- Timeline & owners: propose a 4-week pilot schedule (prep, network config, validation, cutover).

Next steps: fill the attached template and return with network CIDRs + a point-of-contact for VPN setup. We'll schedule a 60-min kickoff with engineering to validate connectivity.

Best,

On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 4:45 PM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Below is a compact boarding checklist you can share with your infra team.

Adding network-specific items we repeatedly see missed during pilots:
- Required ports: outbound TLS 443 for download/telemetry, TCP 22 for admin (optional), and specific ephemeral ports for GPU orchestration (we'll provide a port matrix).
- CIDR guidance: avoid /16 internal ranges that overlap common vendor blocks — provide both production and staging CIDRs.
- NAT & SNAT behavior: confirm whether SNAT will be applied on egress; if so, provide egress NAT IPs for allowlists.
- Healthcheck endpoints: we require an HTTP health port + TCP probe for LB; plan for a dedicated health subnet.
- Peering patterns: prefer route-based peering; for on-prem, IPsec with BGP works best for resilient KV-cache sync.
- MTU & jumbo frames: if sending large model shards, set MTU >= 9000 where possible.

Please see the attached quick reference 'vpc-ip-guidelines.md' for suggested IP ranges and examples.

-Marissa

Ravi — great, thanks for the details and the sheet. Short answers and next steps below.

Answers:
1) BGP flapping: our recommended fallback is to configure a second independent peer (diverse path) and enable session dampening. For state syncing we also support encrypted replication via our out-of-band overlay (falls back to pull + resume if peer disconnects) — we'll share the ops playbook.
2) TLS certs: for pilots we can handle TLS termination at Redwood (managed certs) if you prefer quicker setup; for production we recommend customer-managed certs stored in your KMS/HSM.

Planned next steps:
- Action: HealthSync to return completed 'redwood-onprem-onboard-template.xlsx' with CIDRs, contact list, and KMS owner. Owner: Ravi — due 2026-10-13.
- Action: Redwood to share ops playbook + BGP examples and schedule connectivity runbook review. Owner: Marissa — target 2026-10-11.
- Action: Schedule 60-min kickoff (network + security + infra). I've proposed 2026-10-12 10:00 AM PT — meeting invite to follow.
- Legal/procurement: I'll loop in our GTM/legal TPM after you confirm the DocuSign MSA link — please send when ready.
